guitar.notes: Confirmed — Buddy Guy's polka-dot Fender Stratocaster is one of the most iconic blues guitar associations.

tone.target: wah-led blues lead with gritty Chicago overdrive
tone.profile: wah-led blues lead with gritty Chicago overdrive
tone.summary: A gritty Chicago blues tone using a Boost/OD for drive, Wah for lead sweeps, and an AC30-style amp with vintage cab to capture the raw, cranked tube sound.

rig.name: Buddy Guy - Mary Had A Little Lamb - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and hum.
Provide the necessary gritty Chicago overdrive and single-coil bite.
Implement the central wah sweep for blues lead phrasing.
Add extra raw lead grit and bite without sounding like heavy metal distortion.
blocks.gap: The RAT is often too aggressive, but it provides the necessary 'raw' edge for blues leads.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the cranked tube combo sound (British/American blend) essential for classic blues.
Provide the classic British cabinet sound matching the AC30 tone.
Scoop the low end slightly and boost mids to enhance single-coil bite and presence.
Add subtle movement and width to the lead lines without sounding polished.
blocks.gap: Chorus can sometimes sound too clean, but a low mix adds dimension suitable for blues leads.

blocks.purpose: Provide subtle echo for phrasing without heavy delay or polish.
blocks.gap: The instructions specified 'drop delay,' but Digital Delay is the most versatile choice to keep it minimal and rhythmic.

blocks.purpose: Add a natural sense of space without excessive wash.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism by swapping the generic British IR for a more open, American-voiced speaker to better match the raw Chicago blues grit.

proposals.reason: The AC30 tone needs a more open, American-voiced cab to match the raw Chicago blues grit.
proposals.expectedGain: Increased realism and bite in the upper mids.
